_comment: Expectation manifest for loom's frozen acceptance-checks.
Enforced repo-wide by scripts/evals-all.mjs on every push and PR.
expect "green" = a past fix that must not regress. MUST exit 0.
expect "red"   = a known-failing check (open concern). MUST exit 0 or 1.
A check file missing from this manifest FAILS the gate.
LOCKED (evals/**): improvement loops may never edit this file.

mutations.why: reading invariants from the SUBMITTED graph instead of the approved one is the total bypass: a patch declaring mustCross:[] runs zero dominance checks and validates clean
deleting the structural dominance test lets a bypass edge around a gate validate — this is the single claim loom is sold on
exempting every gate out-edge (not only the locked passing one) readmits `Gate --fail--> Done`, which puts the gate on every path while never satisfying it
dropping the node-budget ceiling lets a patch grow the graph without limit
a permissive guard here skips positional dominance entirely when a patch renames the node the run is standing on — the rename is invisible to structural dominance
dropping positional dominance readmits start -> Gate -> Implement -> terminal: structurally dominated, yet the remaining path never re-crosses the failed gate
routing an unmatched result to the terminal skips EVERY remaining gate — no adversary needed, just a worker returning {passed:'true'} instead of {passed:true}
letting a dead-end node through means the interpreter arrives somewhere with nowhere legal to go and discovers it mid-run instead of before one
mutations.find:
const deadEnds = ids.filter((id) => id !== next.terminal && live.has(id)
    && outEdges(next, id).length === 0);

mutations.why: a clock in the conductor layer breaks resume determinism, and the scan exists to catch exactly that
fs in the conductor layer is the whole prohibition: every side effect belongs in a worker, which has full tools
mutations.replace:
fs.writeFileSync('x', 'y')
let graph   = (args && args.graph)   ? args.graph   : GRAPH_V0

mutations.why: not recording checkSha at freeze time means a worker can weaken the very check it is measured by and the verification reports success
comparing the recorded hash is the whole lock; without it a tampered check file passes verification
a gate whose failing edge leads FORWARD cannot send the run back into real work — which is the only thing loom has over conductor
a DoDBaseline whose out-edge is unconditional advances whether or not the criteria discriminated — the run proceeds on a DoD that could never have failed
without the optimistic-concurrency guard two concurrent saves both return 200 and one edit is silently discarded — the client is told it succeeded while its work is gone
accepting a bare graph body is a documented way to opt out of the guard, and a guard with a supported bypass is not a guard
an unescaped node id reaches innerHTML on the page that IS the human approval gate, turning prompt-injected planner output into 'approve without a human'
dropping SRI lets a CDN serving different bytes tomorrow execute arbitrary code next to the repo it is about to edit
nesting #bar back inside #canvas is the original defect — React clears its mount target, $('save') is null, and the whole approval editor dies on first render
the same failure reached from the other side — moving the mount up to #app swallows every wired element without touching the markup
without the stamp check, mustCross can be set while lockedHash never was — the freeze did not happen, so a patch can MINT locked:true and the exemption rule has nothing behind it
dropping the fingerprint comparison lets a replanner quietly rewrite a locked gate's prompt after approval
a gate told to "Fix every ... and commit" must be caught — that prompt is what suppressed the back-edge 0/3
mutations.find: ADJUDICATE ONLY. Do not fix anything, do not edit files, do not commit.
mutations.replace: Fix every Critical and High finding, keep the build green, and commit.

mutations.why: same regression in the lite seed must not slip through
mutations.find: ADJUDICATE ONLY. Do not fix anything, do not edit files, do not commit.
mutations.replace: Fix every Critical and High finding, keep the build green, and commit.

mutations.why: dropping `findings` back out of required makes the carry optional again — an empty back-edge payload
same regression in the lite seed must not slip through
dropping the one-exit rule lets a region node escape and walk the rest of the graph concurrently with itself
dropping the acyclicity rule admits a dependency cycle, which is a deadlock discovered as a hang mid-run rather than a violation before it
dropping the gate-in-region rule readmits a gate that has nowhere legal to route its own failure
letting a region edge carry a predicate breaks the every-region-node-runs premise the dominance argument rests on
dropping the nested-fork rule admits a region the dataflow runner does not schedule
awaiting each region node in turn produces an identical trace, result and visit counts — the feature becomes decorative while every structural check stays green
mutations.find:
const outs = await parallel(work.map((w) => () =>
        runRegionNode(w.id, w.inst).then((res) => ({ id: w.id + w.inst.suffix, res }))))
mutations.replace:
const outs = []
      for (const w of work) { outs.push(await runRegionNode(w.id, w.inst).then((res) => ({ id: w.id + w.inst.suffix, res }))) }

mutations.why: waiting on every region node instead of a node's own dependencies is a WAVE scheduler: it still looks concurrent, but a node with one dependency is blocked by unrelated slow work
mutations.replace: const preds = [...region].filter((x) => x !== id).flatMap((x) => regionPreds(graph, region, x).length ? [] : outEdges(graph, x).filter((e) => e.to === id || true).slice(0, 1))

mutations.why: parallel() resolves a dead thunk to null rather than rejecting, so removing the guard silently crosses the join with a region node missing and reports the run complete
flat-merging a node's dependency carries lets one dependency silently overwrite another's field, and the node cannot tell which one it is reading
reverting the terminal edge to when:"always" is the original defect — a blocked delivery reporting `complete`
dropping `delivered` from required lets the node omit its verdict entirely
dropping a suggested fix returns the worker to 'you were wrong, work out what to send' — the prose-only rejection this exists to end
a violation that names an edge must expose it as a field; leaving it only inside the sentence forces the caller to parse English
mutations.find:
{ node: e.to, edge: { from: e.from, to: e.to },
          fix: { removeEdges: [{ from: e.from, to: e.to }] } });

mutations.why: a suggested fix that does not actually clear the violation costs the worker a whole visit to discover — worse than offering none
mutations.find:
fix: { removeEdges: [{ from: e.from, to: e.to }],
              addEdges: [Object.assign({}, e, { when: 'always' })] } });
mutations.replace: fix: { removeEdges: [{ from: e.from, to: e.to }] } });

mutations.why: messages() must keep returning the human sentence verbatim, or the editor and CLI render [object Object] at a person
mutations.find: for (const x of violations || []) out.push(x && x.message !== undefined ? x.message : String(x));

mutations.why: truncating to the bound instead of refusing reports success for work that never ran, and looks identical in the report to a run that did everything
mutations.find:
throw new Error('fork ' + node + ' would fan out ' + carried.length + ' times but '
            + 'the approved bound is ' + spec.max + ' — refusing to truncate. Re-approve with '
            + 'a higher fanOut.max, or narrow the list upstream.')

mutations.why: an instance that is not handed its own item gets the same prompt as every other and does identical work N times
accounting instances under the template id makes N instances share one visit budget and starves the last of them
running instances one after another makes the whole feature decorative while every structural check stays green
mutations.find:
const outs = await parallel(work.map((w) => () =>
        runRegionNode(w.id, w.inst).then((res) => ({ id: w.id + w.inst.suffix, res }))))
mutations.replace:
const outs = []
      for (const w of work) { outs.push(await runRegionNode(w.id, w.inst).then((res) => ({ id: w.id + w.inst.suffix, res }))) }

mutations.why: putting `results` back into the checkpoint payload restores the O(n^2): every node re-sends every earlier node's full return value, which was 38% of an observed run
mutations.replace:
graph, cursor, visits, results, carry, trace,
  })

mutations.why: dropping the model opt sends a one-file write to whatever the session runs on — the inherit-not-auto gap this change exists to close
removing the worker's persist instruction turns the whole change into a DELETION of persistence: cheap checkpoints, and every resume replays the run from its start node

keying the strong tier on the LABEL instead of on invariants.mustCross is wrong in both directions at once: a decorative node called "gate" draws the expensive model while a genuinely enforced node labelled "work" adjudicates the terminal on the cheap tier
collapsing the tiers tags every worker with the same model, which looks like a policy in the emitted script and is none
dropping the authored-model override silently upgrades the seeds' deliberately cheap Setup/DoDBaseline nodes and discards a decision a human approved in the graph
applying the policy under `inherit` makes the escape hatch decorative — the one mode that exists to emit nothing would emit everything
computing the policy and never passing it to agent() leaves every worker inheriting while the generator looks correct on inspection
accepting --model-think under inherit lets a caller believe they set a tier that is never read; a flag that cannot take effect must fail loudly
mutations.find:
die(`${flag} requires the auto model mode (it is ignored under --model-mode inherit) — `
        + 'drop the flag or drop --model-mode inherit');

mutations.why: triggering on the "gate" LABEL instead of on invariants.mustCross bills a full plan-check pass for every ordinary non-passing branch in the graph
mutations.find: return must.indexOf(t.node) !== -1 && t.verdict !== true ? t.node : null

mutations.why: routing a NO-GO onward like any other result sends the run straight back into the work plan-check just condemned; instructing the worker to stop is not a guarantee that it did
mutations.find:
const refuted = r && typeof r.refuted === 'number' ? r.refuted : 0
  if (r && (r.planCheck === 'NO-GO' || refuted > 0)) {
    throw new Error('plan-check refused the plan at ' + id + ' (verdict '
      + (r.planCheck || '(none)') + ', ' + refuted + ' REFUTED on a critical path) — refusing '
      + 'to re-implement against a plan just found unsafe. Autofix cannot clear a NO-GO, only '
      + 'shrink one, so this needs a human. Report: ' + (r.report || '(none written)'))
  }

mutations.why: attaching the block to every node makes each first visit pay for a plan-check that nothing has rejected yet
hard-coding the mode ignores --plan-check off, so the one way to opt out of a per-back-edge cost silently does nothing
offering autofix instead of applying it restores the interactive behaviour, which inside an unattended back-edge means no fix is ever applied at all
mutations.find: Run it with AUTOFIX APPLIED, not merely offered.
mutations.replace: Autofix is available if you want it.

mutations.why: trusting only the verdict LABEL leaves the gate resting on a worker correctly recomputing it after autofix; a plan with live REFUTED rows mislabelled GO-WITH-CONDITIONS then sails through the one check meant to stop it
